I have identified and resolved the root causes for both issues in `calc.py`:

   - Fixed the upper boundary check to return `high` instead of `low` when `val > high`.

### 🛠️ Proposed Solution & PR Proposal: Fix SN Open Bounty Radar Parser

Hello Maintainers (@relayhop team),

I have resolved issue #1300 regarding the failure in parsing incoming Stacker News (SN) open bounty telemetry logs.

#### Root Cause
The previous TSV parser was failing on lines with pipe-separated feed strings (`recent@gaming|top@gaming`), comma-separated flag lists (`OPEN_BOUNTY,HOT,SELF_POST_OPP`), and multi-word titles containing UTF-8 emojis.

#### Solution Summary
- Refactored `SnBountyRadarParser` to use a tab-delimited parser with slice-safe title reconstruction.
- Added structured normalization for `feeds` (pipe-split) and `flags` (comma-split).
- Added `isSelfPostOpp` helper flag and explicit NaN fallbacks for numerical fields (`bountySats`, `score`, `userId`).
- Created test coverage covering single and batch parsing scenarios.

#### Contribution & Payment Metadata
- **Contributor**: Jean (@Madatest)
- **Bounty Payout Channel**: Algora / Escrow / Binance Pay UID `254779310` (0% Fee option)

Ready to open the PR immediately upon maintainer confirmation.

top_opportunities.title: [Security]: Policy/allowlist bypass via scheduled lane: schedule_stream / execute_scheduled skip check_asset_allowed and validate_stream_args
top_opportunities.description:
### Severity (self-assessed)

Critical

### Affected component

contract (Rust)

### Impact class

Funds drainable

### Summary

The policy module is the on-chain allowlist: create_stream enforces check_asset_allowed and reverts PolicyAssetNotAllowed (#31) for blocked assets. The scheduled lane never calls it — schedule.rs contains zero references to "policy", and neither schedule_stream nor execute_scheduled invokes check_asset_allowed or validate_stream_args. A permissionless sender can therefore open streams (with escrow) for assets the admin explicitly blocked — e.g. scam or sanctioned tokens — while simultaneously bypassing min-deposit / duration / rate floors and the protocol fee. The team's own exemption list (POLICY_GOVERNANCE.md L32) covers only withdraw / withdraw_max / cancel_stream; the scheduled lane appears in no exemption.


### Reproduction

NET="--network testnet"
CID="--id CCF6M73DGUWTDKXE76FKZJIFKHAK3CMUJPTZIXSBXYG4Z5CUS5PUSLKE"
# Own testnet deployment of the pinned commit (wasm sha256 4a5c771e...c94bd616).
# Replace --source identities with funded testnet accounts.

# 1. Initialize policy and block FZNB (CCNZ27...QIGWJ)
stellar contract invoke $NET $CID --source gov -- policy_init --admin GAJ6HLMKKFF5GXX2PAT7WUZ53PATELHT4I5L5XR2YTJAXQE4IHPF4XLX
stellar contract invoke $NET $CID --source gov -- policy_set_timelock_delay --delay 0
stellar contract invoke $NET $CID --source gov -- policy_propose_asset --asset CCNZ27KWIOQC3S5MO4MWNDDRN2EB3L4KLOHWRK4AQ7ACIFCVNBHQIGWJ --allowed false
stellar contract invoke $NET $CID --source gov -- policy_execute_asset --asset CCNZ27KWIOQC3S5MO4MWNDDRN2EB3L4KLOHWRK4AQ7ACIFCVNBHQIGWJ

# 2. State proof: asset is blocked
stellar contract invoke $NET $CID --source gov -- policy_is_asset_allowed --asset CCNZ27KWIOQC3S5MO4MWNDDRN2EB3L4KLOHWRK4AQ7ACIFCVNBHQIGWJ
# expected: false
# actual:   false

# 3. NEGATIVE CONTROL — direct lane still enforces the policy
stellar contract invoke $NET $CID --source sender -- create_stream

top_opportunities.title: [Security]: freeze-logic trigger
top_opportunities.description:
### Severity (self-assessed)

High

### Affected component

contract (Rust)

### Impact class

Invariant break

### Summary

The emergency freeze is enforced via require_not_frozen on all five direct-lane entrypoints (create_stream, create_streams, withdraw, top_up, update_rates) — each reverts ContractFrozen while frozen. The scheduled-intents lane has zero references to `frozen`: while the admin has the contract frozen, any permissionless caller can schedule_stream (new funds enter escrow during the freeze), execute_scheduled (state transitions continue during the freeze, keeper fees still paid), plus cancel_scheduled / reclaim_expired. The freeze — the incident-response brake — therefore does not hold on one lane.


### Reproduction

NET="--network testnet"
CID="--id CCF6M73DGUWTDKXE76FKZJIFKHAK3CMUJPTZIXSBXYG4Z5CUS5PUSLKE"
# Own testnet deployment of the pinned commit (wasm sha256 4a5c771e...c94bd616).

stellar contract invoke $NET $CID --source gov -- is_frozen

top_opportunities.title: [soundness] const identifier alias bypasses HYB-E6002: const big = 300; var n int8 = big passes hyb check, emitted Go fails go build
top_opportunities.description:
### The smallest .hy program that demonstrates it

```hy
// const-alias.hy (commit 422066b, main 2026-10-17)
const big = 300

fn main() {
    var n int8 = big
    fmt.println("{n}")
}
```

`hyb check` on `422066b`: `OK (0 diagnostics)`. The emitted Go fails `go build`:
`./a.out.go:10:15: cannot use big (untyped int constant 300) as int8 value in variable declaration (overflows)`.

The literal form `var n int8 = 300` is already rejected by the landed E6002 fix (#148/#201-B) — this
is the identifier form of the same rule, and it currently slips through because the E6002 fold never
resolves file-level `const` names to their initializers.

Exact commands (unpatched clean `422066b` checker):

```
$ hyb check const-alias.hy
const-alias.hy: OK (0 diagnostics)

$ hyb build const-alias.hy --emit-go      # emits a.out.go
$ go build a.out.go
./a.out.go:10:15: cannot use big (untyped int constant 300) as int8 value in variable declaration (overflows)
```

With the fix (`0f05024`):

```
$ hyb check const-alias.hy
error[HYB-E6002]: constant `big` overflows declared type `int8` of `n` (HYB-E6002)
```

### What the checker should say

Reject with **HYB-E6002** at the initializer, as it already does for the literal:
``constant `big` overflows declared type `int8` of `n` ``. Go requires the constant identifier's
value to fit the declared fixed-width type. A local binding with the same name shadows the const
and must not be resolved.

### What it actually said

`OK (0 diagnostics)`, then the emitted Go is rejected. Root cause:
`const_overflow.rs::const_int_fold` folds only int literals, unary `-`, and arithmetic operators; it
has no `Expr::Ident` arm, even though the checker holds every file-level const binding. Every
context that routes through the fold (including the per-context checks in the open conveyor
#515/#520/#526/#528/#530) is therefore launderable by a const alias.

### Claimed severity

P2 — claim-precision bug (accepted value should have been unproven)

### Anything else

## Bounty: ultrank_11_20 — 250 frames (label from scratch) [1/6]

Create labels for **250** frames from `ultrank_11_20`. This dataset has no labels yet, so you are the source of truth — the model's boxes are a starting point, not an answer.

**How to claim**

Comment `claim` on this issue. Then run `python scripts/bounty.py start `.

**What to do**

- Open each frame. The dashed boxes are the model's guesses.
- Press `a` to adopt them all, then fix what is wrong; or press `d` to draw by hand.
- Every player gets exactly one tight box. Press `g` when the frame is correct.
- Press `n` on menus, results screens and other non-gameplay frames.
- Push your labels and open a PR that says `Closes #`.

**Reward:** 318 points (250 frames × 1.27 difficulty)
